Here are a few dinner ideas built around what's actually in your garden right now — cherry tomatoes, basil, mint, and peppers — and matched to what you've been cooking lately:

**Top pick: Braised chicken thighs with cherry tomato and basil sauce**
You've been practising braising and just made a red wine braise with cremini mushrooms, so this is a natural next step. Sear chicken thighs, then braise them in a sauce of crushed cherry tomatoes, garlic, and a generous handful of torn basil. The tomatoes break down into a rich, slightly sweet sauce; the basil goes in at the end so it stays bright. Serve over the Italian herb sourdough you're developing — the rosemary and roasted garlic in it would complement the tomato-basil sauce well.

**If you want something lighter: Grilled peppers and cherry tomato salad with mint-basil dressing**
Slice the peppers (once the aphids are under control), blister or grill them, and toss with halved cherry tomatoes. Make a quick dressing with mint, basil, olive oil, lemon, and a pinch of salt. This uses all four of your homegrown ingredients and is the kind of easy, affordable plate you've said you prefer.

**If you're in an Indian-cooking mood: Pepper and tomato curry with mint chutney**
You've been cooking Indian food at home and made a chicken tikka masala that came out well. A simple pepper-and-tomato curry (with onion, garlic, cumin, and a little cayenne) uses your peppers and cherry tomatoes as the base, and a fresh mint chutney on the side gives the mint a purpose. Serve with naan — you're already working on getting it to puff up properly, so this is a good test.

**A small note on the peppers:** your pepper plants still have the aphid issue, so if you harvest from them this weekend, give the fruit a good rinse and check for any remaining insects before cooking.

All three options stay within your easy-and-affordable preference and use ingredients you already have growing. The braise is the one that most directly builds on what you've been practising in your cooking classes.
